brief: Overnight: US equity futures rally, UST yields hold onto gains, and crude retreats as European countries (France specifically) discuss releasing diesel/crude stockpiles. Attention turns to today's NFP: GIR forecasts September payrolls at 80k, below the 88k consensus but above the 71k three-month average, because a late Labor Day and non-repeating August strength in education/leisure-hospitality argue for payback; unemployment is seen dipping to 4.0% on falling continuing claims even as GIR's own slack tracker (4.6%) implies labor is softer than that headline suggests. Separately, GIR's credit desk says IG/HY spreads widened toward quarter-end forecasts (80bp/311bp) after a resilient September, sees risk tilted toward further widening into December absent a growth shock, and cuts the 2026 USD HY issuance forecast to $340bn from $400bn as AI-related project financing grows. A third piece argues oil is the best vehicle for both tail risks (escalation and relief) because its implied vol hasn't reset, favoring protected long-equity positioning. The Financials section is a broad single-name roundup: a CBOE upgrade, a Fannie/Freddie credit-bureau data change, capital-markets sector picks, and REIT acquisitions (CTRE, FRT).
